How to Use the Assembly Info Builder

A step-by-step guide. No computer skills needed — if you can fill out a form online, you can do this.

1What is this?

The Assembly Info Builder helps you put together one simple page for your volunteers: who is assigned where, the schedules, important phone numbers, notes, and maps — for each department (Parking, Cleaning, Stage, Seating, and so on).

When you're done, you press one button and get a file you can text or email to every volunteer. They open it on their phone and everything is right there — no app to install, no internet needed once they have it.

There are two kinds of files. Don't mix them up!

  • The Builder (your working copy). This is where you type everything in. Think of it as your master notebook. Keep it to yourself.
  • The Volunteer file. This is the handout. It's made by the Builder when you press 📱 Export for Volunteers. Volunteers can look at it but cannot change it.

2Opening the Builder

Find the file called Assembly Info Builder (or a file ending in PROJECT (master) if someone handed one to you) and double-click it. It opens in your web browser — the same program you use for websites, like Chrome, Edge, or Safari.

That's it. There is nothing to install and nothing to sign up for.

The top of the Builder. The three buttons in the dark bar are the most important ones.

The three buttons at the top:

  • ✨ New Event — start over with a blank event (it will warn you first).
  • 💾 Save Project File — saves your master notebook as a file. Press this when you finish working. More on this in section 8 — it's the most important habit in this whole guide.
  • 📱 Export for Volunteers — makes the handout file you send to volunteers.

3Set up your event

At the top of the page, fill in the basics — just click in a box and type:

  • Event title — for example, "2027 Regional Convention".
  • Subtitle — a small line under the title, like "Volunteer Reference".
  • Footer note — a short message shown at the very bottom of every page.
  • Days of the event — normally Friday, Saturday, Sunday. You can rename a day by clicking its name, remove one with the little ×, or press + Add day.

4Groups (departments)

Each department gets its own group — its own page in the volunteer handout. Volunteers tap a department name at the top of the page to switch between them, and swipe left and right to move between the days.

Click a group name to work on it. The one you're working on is highlighted.
  • + Add group — makes a new department. Type its name (like "First Aid") when asked.
  • The colored dots — the group's color, used on its tab and headings. Click any dot, or click the rainbow circle at the end to choose any color you like (your organization's color, a color that matches a sign, anything). The little chip to the right shows exactly how the group name will look to volunteers.
  • ◀ and ▶ — change the order of the groups. This is the order the department buttons appear in for volunteers.
  • Delete group — removes the whole department. It will ask you to confirm first.

5Filling in names, assignments, and schedules

Below the group buttons you'll see Friday / Saturday / Sunday tabs, and then the group's content in boxes called sections. Each section has a small label in its corner telling you what kind it is.

Day tabs at the top, then sections. Here: a Contact List, then an Assignment Roster.

The day tabs matter!

Assignments and schedules can be different on each day. The day tab that is dark is the day you are editing right now. Fill in Friday first, then use the Copy Friday to all other days button — it copies everything to Saturday and Sunday so you only have to fix the differences.

Typing names the easy way

When you click in a Name box and start typing, a little list of names appears — these come from the Volunteer Directory (section 6). Pick the name instead of typing it all out. Two nice things happen:

  • The name is always spelled the same way everywhere.
  • If the row has a Phone box and it's empty, the phone number fills in by itself.
A schedule: each row is a time, a person, and their phone number.
Tip: the little × at the end of a row removes that row. The dashed buttons like + Add person add a new empty row.

WhatsApp numbers

Next to each Phone box there's a WhatsApp box. On site, people often reach each other on WhatsApp because regular calls get ignored as spam, so volunteers will see a green WhatsApp button next to the phone number and can tap whichever they prefer.

  • If WhatsApp is on the same number, click the small = button — it copies the phone number across.
  • If it's a different number, just type that number instead.
  • If the person doesn't use WhatsApp, leave the box empty — no button will show for them.
  • You can also paste a WhatsApp link (one that starts with wa.me) if you have one.
You only have to enter it once. Put a person's WhatsApp in the Volunteer Directory and it is used everywhere else that person appears — schedules and contact lists included. Those boxes will show a grey hint like from directory: 816-555-0101 so you know the button will appear. Only type in the box if that person needs a different number in that spot.

6The Volunteer Directory

The directory is the full list of everyone in the department, with their phone number, what they do, and any special notes (like "mornings only"). Fill this in first — then their names are pickable everywhere else, in every group.

Each person gets a name, phone, assignment, and (if needed) a note about limitations.
Tip: don't worry about putting people in alphabetical order — the volunteer handout sorts them automatically, and volunteers get a search box.

7Adding pictures and maps

In an Images / Maps section, press + Attach image(s)… and choose pictures from your computer or phone. Type a short caption under each one. Volunteers can tap a picture to see it full-screen.

Pictures are automatically shrunk so the final file stays small enough to text.

Want a section a group doesn't have yet?

Scroll to the bottom of the group. There's a box of six section types — click one to add it. You can also rename any section by clicking its title, move it up or down with the ▲ ▼ arrows, or remove it with the ×.

The six kinds of sections you can add to any group.

8Saving your work — read this part!

The Builder saves as you type, but only inside the browser on the computer you're using. To make a real, permanent copy you can keep, move, or hand to someone else:

  1. Press 💾 Save Project File.
  2. A file downloads, named something like "Your Event - PROJECT (master).html".
  3. Keep that file somewhere safe — it IS your master notebook. Opening it later brings everything back exactly as you left it.
Important: press Save Project File every time you finish working, the same way you'd save a document. If the computer is cleaned up or you switch computers, that saved file is the only copy of your work.

9Sending it to your volunteers

When everything looks right, press 📱 Export for Volunteers. A file downloads, named something like "Your Event - Volunteer Info.html". Send that file to your volunteers by text message or email — that's the whole job.

Here is what volunteers see when they open it on their phone:

Tip: volunteers can't change anything in this file — so send it freely. If something changes later, just fix it in the Builder and send out a fresh copy.

10Sharing the work with department captains

You don't have to type in every department yourself. Each captain can fill in their own department:

  1. Give each captain a copy of the Builder file.
  2. The captain fills in their group only — schedules, assignments, directory.
  3. The captain clicks the small ⇪ Export group JSON button (it's in the row with the colored dots) and sends you the little file it downloads.
  4. You click 📥 Import group JSON… (next to "+ Add group") and pick their file. Their whole department drops right into your master copy.
Note about pictures: pictures do not travel inside those little files — that's on purpose, for safety. After importing, any picture spots will say "missing — click to attach", and you attach the pictures yourself.
Tip: agree on the group name ahead of time (for example, exactly "Parking"). If you import a group with the same name as one you already have, the Builder asks whether to replace it — that's normally what you want when a captain sends an updated version.

11Common questions

I made a mistake. Is there an undo button?
No — but almost everything asks "are you sure?" before deleting. If something big goes wrong, close without saving and open your last saved PROJECT (master) file: it has everything from your last save.
I opened the Builder and my work isn't there!
You are probably on a different computer or a different browser. Your work lives in the saved PROJECT (master) file — find the newest one and open that instead.
The name list doesn't suggest the person I want.
They aren't in a Volunteer Directory yet. Add them to the directory first — or just type their name in full; typing always works.
A phone number filled in wrong.
Just click in the phone box and fix it. The automatic fill only happens when the phone box is empty — it never overwrites what you type.
I picked a color but it looks slightly different on the page.
Some colors — very bright pinks and greens especially — don't leave enough contrast for the group name to be readable on top of them. When that happens the app darkens or lightens the color just enough to keep the name legible. The preview chip next to the color dots always shows you the real result.
Can volunteers change the file I send them?
No. The volunteer file is view-only. All editing happens in the Builder.
How do I start next year's event without retyping everyone?
Open this year's master file, change the title and dates, update the assignments, and press Save Project File — it downloads as a new file, so this year's copy stays untouched.
